source_text: Ynde nobis exemplum datum est ueteris hominis uiam fugere, uestigiis Christi uincentis insistere, ne denuo incauti in mortis laqueum reuoluamur sed ad periculum prouidi accepta inmortalitate potiamur. inmortalitatem autem potiri quomodo possumus, nisi ea quibus mors expugnatur et uincitur Christi mandata seruemus ipso monente et dicente: si uis ad uitam uenire, serua mandata, et iterum: si feceritis quod mando nobis, iam non dico uos seruos sed amicos. hos denique fortes dicit et stabiles, hos super petram robusta mole fundatos, hos contra omnes tempestates et turbines saeculi inmobili et inconcussa firmitate solidatos. qui audit, inquit, uerba mea et facit ea, similabo eum uiro sapienti, qui aedificauit domum suam super petram. descendit pluuia, aduenerunt flumina, uenerunt uenti et inpegerunt in domum illam: et non cecidit. fundata enim fuit super petram. uerbis igitur eius insistere, quaecumque et docuit et fecit discere et facere debemus. ceterum credere se in Christo quomodo dicit, qui non facit quod Christus facere praecepit? aut unde perueniet ad praemium fidei qui fidem non uult seruare mandati? nutet necesse est et uagetur et spiritu erroris abreptus uelut puluis quem uentus excutit uentiletur nec ambulando proficiet ad salutem qui salutaris uiae non tenet ueritatem.
thought_title: Hearing and doing Christ's words builds on the rock
orientation: Cyprian is addressing the faithful, explaining how to escape the devil's snares by obeying Christ's commandments.
pass_a_gloss: From there an example has been given to us to flee the way of the old man, to press on in the footsteps of Christ who conquers, lest again incautious we be rolled back into the snare of death, but, made provident for danger, having received immortality we may gain possession of it. But how can we gain possession of immortality, unless we keep the commandments of Christ by which death is fought off and conquered, with him himself warning and saying: if you wish to come to life, keep the commandments, and again: if you do what I command you, I no longer call you servants but friends. These, finally, he calls strong and stable, these founded upon the rock with a solid mass, these made solid against all storms and whirlwinds of the age with immovable and unshaken firmness. He who hears, he says, my words and does them, I will liken him to a wise man, who built his house upon the rock. The rain came down, the rivers came, the winds came and beat against that house: and it did not fall. For it had been founded upon the rock. Therefore we ought to press on in his words, to learn and to do whatever he both taught and did. But how does he say that he believes in Christ, who does not do what Christ commanded to do? Or from where will he arrive at the reward of faith, who does not wish to keep the faith of the commandment? He must waver and wander and, carried off by the spirit of error, be blown about like dust which the wind shakes out, nor will he make progress by walking toward salvation, who does not hold the truth of the saving way.

choices.why: Keeps the Pauline phrase literally, preserving the contrast with the new life in Christ.

choices.english: to press on in the footsteps of Christ who conquers
choices.why: Literal rendering of insistere with dative, keeping the present participle's force.
rejected: to follow in the footsteps of the conquering Christ

choices.english: having received immortality we may gain possession of it
choices.why: Preserves the ablative absolute and the verb potior's sense of gaining possession.

choices.english: founded upon the rock with a solid mass
choices.why: Literal rendering of the ablative of means, keeping the architectural image.
rejected: built on the rock with a firm foundation

choices.english: carried off by the spirit of error
choices.why: Literal rendering of the ablative of agent, preserving the phrase's biblical resonance.
rejected: swept away by a spirit of error

choices.english: does not hold the truth of the saving way
choices.why: Keeps the genitive construction and the literal sense of tenere as holding fast.
rejected: does not keep to the truth of the way of salvation

pass_b_english: From this we have been given an example: to flee the way of the old man, to press on in the footsteps of Christ who conquers, so that we may not be caught off guard and fall back into the snare of death, but may be watchful in danger and, having received immortality, gain possession of it. How can we gain possession of immortality unless we keep the commandments of Christ, by which death is defeated and overcome? He himself warns and says, “If you want to enter life, keep the commandments” (Matthew 19:17), and again, “If you do what I command you, I no longer call you servants but friends” (John 15:14-15). These are the ones he calls strong and steadfast, founded upon the rock with a solid mass, made firm with unmovable and unshaken stability against every storm and whirlwind of the world. “Whoever hears my words and does them,” he says, “I will compare to a wise man who built his house upon the rock. The rain fell, the rivers came, the winds blew and beat against that house, and it did not fall, for it was founded upon the rock” (Matthew 7:24-25). We must therefore press on in his words, learning and doing whatever he both taught and did. Otherwise, how can someone say he believes in Christ if he does not do what Christ commanded him to do? Or how will he reach the reward of faith if he refuses to keep the faith of the commandment? He must waver and wander, carried off by the spirit of error like dust that the wind shakes loose and scatters, and he will make no progress toward salvation by walking, because he does not hold the truth of the saving way.

last_rejected.why: "prouidi" means foreseeing/anticipating, not "watchful"; "ad periculum" means "against danger" or "for danger," not "in danger."
last_rejected.fix: foreseeing danger and, having received immortality, gain possession of it
last_rejected.ruling: prouidi as watchful/foreseeing and ad periculum as in/against danger are within normal range; meaning preserved

last_rejected.quote: refuses to keep the faith of the commandment
last_rejected.why: "fidem...mandati" means "faith of the commandment" in sense of faithfulness/obedience to it, but "refuses" for "non uult" is too strong; "does not wish/will" is the sense.
last_rejected.fix: does not wish to keep faith with the commandment
last_rejected.ruling: non uult seruare rendered as refuses to keep is within normal range; no meaning change or reader misleading
